description: Raw mouse input with no acceleration and no smoothing (B0015, B0017, B0018). A thread of its own reads the mouse's raw input (WM_INPUT, device counts, 64-bit counters), so Windows' pointer speed and acceleration, the screen edges and the frame rate no longer change how far the view turns, and high polling rates cost the game nothing; menus keep the cursor. cl_mouseAccel and m_filter have no effect. A 0 ms frame keeps the movement for the next frame, and the yaw is kept within [-180, 180). Store build only, loaded into the game by runtime/loader (docs/enhanced-build.md).

description: Mouse sensitivity in MW2019's units: m_sens (default 1.5, 0.01 to 100, archived, registered on first use) turns the view by m_sens * 0.0066 degrees per count at any field of view, hip fire and aiming down sights alike; the profile's sensitivity, the FOV scale and m_yaw no longer apply to the mouse, m_pitch's sign still inverts. The view angles are kept in double precision between frames. Store build only.

description: Key events on the game's clock, timed to the millisecond (B0019, B0020). Before the game's window procedure handles a message, g_wv.sysMsgTime (the time its queued events carry) is set on the game's clock (timeGetTime - sys_timeBase): for a key, the time the raw input thread saw that key change; for anything else, or a key it didn't see, the message's time moved onto the game's clock. A movement key's press and release frames now count the part of the frame it was held. Also keeps Windows 11 from dropping the game's 1 ms timer while its window is minimized or covered. Store build only.
